title: scripts/check.ps1 and scripts/check.sh may assert only causes they have established
evaluation_level_rationale: These two scripts are the local gate every builder reads before reporting, and the defect class under repair is a report that is wrong in the ALARMING direction. A wrong summary here has already caused three false alarms on this project; a builder acting on 'a secret was found' could edit .secrets.baseline and do real damage. Level 2 because the correction must be proven in BOTH directions per branch, not merely reviewed.
objective: Remove, from both check scripts, every place where a non-zero exit status is translated into a specific stated cause the script has not established. For each such branch either establish the cause before naming it, or surface the underlying tool's own output and report only the status actually observed.
measured_premise: REPORTED DEFECT, reproduced by reading: scripts/check.ps1 maps detect-secrets-hook exit 1 to the single sentence 'a secret that is not in the baseline was found'. Exit 1 is also what the hook returns for an unstaged baseline, an unreadable baseline and other argument errors, so the sentence is an assertion the script has not established.

MEASURED on this host: `detect-secrets-hook --baseline .secrets.baseline` with ZERO filenames exits 0 (bare read of $LASTEXITCODE). Both scripts build the file list from git and pass it through unchecked, so a git failure yields an empty list and the scan reports PASS having scanned nothing. That is the same defect pointing the reassuring way.

MEASURED on this host: PowerShell 7.6.5 with $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = False, so the exit-code switch in check.ps1 is genuinely reached. The switch is not dead code here, but the script's reliance on an ambient $LASTEXITCODE is host-dependent, so the fix reads status from an explicitly captured value instead.

MEASURED: this worktree began with no .venv and no node_modules, which is exactly the impostor condition recorded in agent-state/progress.md where check.ps1 reported 'Prettier check, ESLint FAILING' whose real cause was absent npm dependencies.

MEASURED with tests/support/source_scan.py on the untouched files: block depth immediately before the scripts/check_secrets_baseline.py invocation is 0 in BOTH scripts (check.sh line 102, check.ps1 line 68), and the scanner blanks string bodies. The protected guard's unconditional-top-level-early-exit case therefore requires that invocation to stay at depth 0; this contract keeps it there and re-measures after editing.
out_of_scope_zero_diff: agent-state/feature_list.json - must stay byte-identical, verified by git hash-object

.github/workflows/ci.yml - CARRIES THE SAME DEFECT at line 143 ('detect-secrets found a secret that is not in the baseline') and is owned by a concurrent builder in this dispatch. Reported, deliberately not repaired, to avoid a collision. Must stay byte-identical.
.secrets.baseline - not refreshed unless a tracked file is added
every application source file under apps/
acceptance_criteria: AC1 - No branch in either script states a cause it has not established. Every remaining stated cause is either measured by the script itself or is the underlying tool's own output quoted back.
AC2 - detect-secrets exit 1 no longer asserts that a secret was found. The hook's own stdout and stderr are surfaced and the reported status is the one actually observed.
AC3 - A baseline REWRITE is named only when the script has established it, by comparing the digest of .secrets.baseline before and after the run, rather than inferring it from an exit code alone.
AC4 - An empty scan file list fails with that as its stated cause instead of passing vacuously.
AC5 - A missing external tool fails with 'not found in .venv nor on PATH' as its stated cause, established by resolution, not inferred from a non-zero exit.
AC6 - Absent node_modules fails as a missing-dependency condition with its own cause, not as a Prettier or ESLint failure.
AC7 - The exit status a check reports is one the check established. A stale ambient exit code can never be reported as this check's result.
AC8 - No check is weakened. Every condition that failed before still fails; only the stated cause changes.
AC9 - Both scripts remain accepted by tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py, including the unconditional-top-level-early-exit case, with those two test files unmodified.
AC10 - For every corrected branch, BOTH directions are demonstrated: the genuine failure still fails with a true message, and the impostor condition reports its own cause.
negative_and_regression_tests: Genuine secret planted in a tracked file: Secret scan must still FAIL, and the message must be true.
Unstaged .secrets.baseline: Secret scan must FAIL reporting the hook's own words, not a secret finding.
Empty file list: Secret scan must FAIL rather than pass.
Baseline actually rewritten by the hook: the rewrite must be named, and established by digest change.
node_modules removed: Prettier and ESLint must report the missing dependency, not a formatting or lint verdict.
node_modules present and a genuinely mis-formatted file: Prettier must still FAIL as a formatting failure.
Tool absent from PATH and .venv: the check must FAIL naming the unresolved tool.
Tool present and genuinely failing: the check must still FAIL on the tool's own status.
Full green run: with every prerequisite present and the tree clean, both scripts must still report all checks passed.
tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py - 141 tests, green before and after.
verification_commands: git hash-object <protected paths> compared against the same paths at 5a3fb24
data_security_privacy_portability_z0: No product behaviour changes. No Z0 rule, quota, classification, schema, migration, endpoint or dependency is touched. No network access is added. No credential or internal package-feed hostname may reach any file, report, commit message or PR body. Portability is improved rather than reduced: the PowerShell script stops depending on an ambient $LASTEXITCODE whose propagation differs across PowerShell versions.
reporting_rule_location: The rule this slice enforces is written into the .NOTES/header of each script rather than a separate document, so it sits where a reader of the branch is standing. No new docs file was added; the in_scope entry that anticipated one was withdrawn rather than satisfied decoratively.
findings_reported_not_repaired: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 143 carries the IDENTICAL defect being repaired here - it maps detect-secrets exit 1 to 'detect-secrets found a secret that is not in the baseline.' CI runs on Linux, so the false alarm is still live there. Owned by a concurrent builder in this dispatch; reported rather than repaired to avoid a collision.

The ESLint check is very close to vacuous. MEASURED: root eslint.config.js sets ignores: [..., 'apps/web/'], and `eslint . --format json` returns exactly ONE linted file, eslint.config.js itself. apps/web has its own eslint.config.js and lint script that NOTHING invokes - not check.ps1, not check.sh, not ci.yml (which runs the same root `npm run lint`). Proven in both directions: an identical no-undef error exits 1 at repo root and exits 0 inside apps/web/src. The check is not literally unfailable, but it cannot fail on any defect in the web application. Same shape on the sibling check: .prettierignore also excludes apps/web/.

scripts/check.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml build the scan list from `git ls-files -z` (TRACKED ONLY) while scripts/check.ps1 uses `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` (tracked AND untracked). MEASURED: a secret in an untracked file is seen by check.ps1 and NOT by check.sh. The bash route therefore matches CI and check.ps1 is the stricter outlier. Reported, deliberately not changed: altering what a check COVERS is a scope change, and it would make check.sh diverge from the CI it claims to mirror.
boundary: Draft PR only. Do not merge. Do not modify agent-state/feature_list.json. Do not modify .github/workflows/ci.yml, tests/support/source_scan.py or tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py.
